fermentation.verdict: One teacher you can name, in a room you can book, in Tokyo — and nowhere else yet. Thin, and we would rather say so

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Yes in Tokyo: &LAB TOKYO's own page says Chie Ando teaches the course in person, and names her. Copenhagen came off this map on 6 November 2026: its one summer day at noma Projects is sold only to members, and the distillery once listed there has moved to Brooklyn and runs no course.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Yes. &LAB TOKYO takes a stranger directly and arranges the dates when you apply; its three-day intensive is ¥156,000 before tax, taught in Japanese, with English support at ¥15,000 a day.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Not reliably. &LAB's groups are one to four, so you may well be alone with the teacher, which is good teaching and no company.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Not answered. Everything we have comes from the school selling the course, and that cannot tell you whether the craft lives in the city around it.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been, and no body publishes a ladder for fermentation: a school's own certificate is the most there is.

bread-and-boulangerie.verdict: Real doors, in English and in French, with dates and prices on them — and not one teacher we have yet named from a page we read

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Not yet, on our own reading. The École Internationale de Boulangerie names its founder, Thomas Teffri-Chambelland, but a founder is not a teacher. FERRANDI Paris and the École de Boulangerie et de Pâtisserie de Paris name nobody on the course pages we read on 4 November 2026. Ask who will be in the bakery with you.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Yes. FERRANDI Paris runs twelve weeks of bread and viennoiseries in English, 25 August to 19 November 2027, at €18,500. The École de Boulangerie et de Pâtisserie de Paris runs its CAP route from September, in French only and only for EU or Swiss nationals or holders of a work permit. In Copenhagen, Meyers Madhus sells one-day classes in English with dates on them.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Yes. These are classes, not private lessons: the Paris CAP takes forty-eight a year in groups of twelve at the bench, and Meyers seats sixteen.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Not answered. Everything here comes from the schools themselves. A guild, a market or a bakers' competition would answer it, and we have not read one yet.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been. The ladder exists in public — the CAP Boulanger is a state diploma with a published référentiel — and we have not adopted it on this page yet.

modern-new-technique-cuisine.verdict: Named teachers in most of the rooms, and now the Spanish ones too — a toolkit you can learn anywhere, beside the places that invented it

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Yes in five of the six places, each a named living person: Martin Lippo at Vakuum in Barcelona, Éric Briffard at Le Cordon Bleu Paris, Miguel Ángel Cepeda in Puebla and Mexico City, Luis Arrufat with Txema Urda on the Basque Culinary Center's online course, and in Madrid the chefs Le Cordon Bleu names on its own Meet the Chefs page, read 17 September 2026 — Natalia Vázquez with David Vela, Manuel Lucas and Diego Muñoz. Sous Vide Australia now trains a venue's own team rather than the public. ⛔ Where we stand: EducatedTraveler ran a paid week with Martin Lippo in October 2026, so we are not a neutral party about him. Nobody pays to be on this map and no money reaches us from him; the way in without us is his own site, martinlippo.com.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open, and unusually so for the avant-garde. Private courses at Vakuum (his classroom courses for 2026 are sold out and no later date is shown, read 4 November 2026), four days in Paris with English translation as it is taught, a diplomado in Mexico, five weeks or an online course in San Sebastián, and the avant-garde third of a nine-month diploma in Madrid. Kitchen stages are not listed here: Arnaud's ruling of 4 November 2026 took them off the map, because you cannot book one. The hands can ruin it — a spherification bath and liquid nitrogen are unforgiving.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Yes, on the Paris course, the diplomado and the diplomas, which run as classes rather than as private hire. At Vakuum the way in is now a private course. The group size is published almost nowhere, and in a technique lab it decides whether you touch the equipment or watch it. Ask before you book.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes in Spain, and that is what changed. The toolkit travels — sous-vide was worked out at Troisgros in 1974 and belongs to every kitchen with a circulator — but Madrid Fusión has been the vanguard's own congress since 2003, and it meets in Madrid, which is now one of this craft's places. The places outside Spain are here for the toolkit; the ones inside it are here for the argument.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been, and no single body publishes a ladder: the qualification is a school's certificate, or in Madrid a diploma. What happens after the course is up to you and your own kitchen.
